# The Authors

::: {.author-card}
::: {.author-info}
## R. Douglas Martin {.unnumbered}

Doug Martin is Professor Emeritus in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics at the University of Washington and a founder of the Computational Finance and Risk Managment (CFRM) program. He co-founded two software firms - Statistical Sciences Inc (the S+ company) and Finanalytica, and was involved in porting the S+ `robust` package to R. In addition, he has co-authored two textbooks: *Modern Portfolio Optimization* (with Bernd Scherer) and *Robust Statistics : Theory and Methods* (with Ricardo Maronna, Victor Yohai and Matias Salibian-Barrera).
:::
:::

::: {.author-card}
::: {.author-info}
## Thomas K. Philips {.unnumbered}

Thomas Philips is an Adjunct Professor in the Department of Finance and Risk Engineering at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering. Prior to teaching Portfolio Managment and Valuation for Startups and Corporate Transactions at Tandon, he was the Global Head of Front Office Risk for the Institutional Division of BNP Paribas Investment Partners. He was awarded the First Bernstein/Fabozzi/Jacobs-Levy Prize for his paper *Why Do Valuation Ratios Forecast Long-Run Equity Returns?* and the Graham and Dodd Scroll Award for *Saving Social Security: A Better Approach* (co-authored with Arun Muralidhar).
:::
:::

::: {.author-card}
::: {.author-info}
## Bernd Scherer {.unnumbered}

Bernd Scherer is the Head of Portfolio Implementation at the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) and is on the Advisory Board of EDHEC’s Ph.D. in Finance program where he served as Professor of Finance and Head of the European Master's in Finance program.  He is currently on the editorial board of the Financial Analysts Journal and the Journal of Asset Management. Before joining ADIA, he was CIO at LBBW Asset Management, where he was responsible for 110 billion assets under management. He was twice awarded the best paper award from EQD and one from the German CFA society and was named to be among the top 25 quants worldwide by EQD.
:::
:::

::: {.author-card}
::: {.author-info}
## Kirk Li {.unnumbered}

Kirk Li is a Principal Machine Learning Science Manager at Microsoft. He earned his Ph.D. in Statistics from the University of Washington.
:::
:::

# About This Book

*Robust Portfolio Construction and Risk Analysis* (RPCRA) is a graduate-level textbook providing a rigorous, unified treatment of quantitative portfolio management techniques that are designed to work in the presence of noise. It is distinguished by its focus on reproducibility, and its companion `PCRA` package contains data sets that support reproducibility as which may also be used by course instructors to create new exercises. 

The book integrates the classical theory of mean-variance optimization, including the estimation of expected returns and the measurement of risk and performance, with robust statistical methods for parameter estimation, regression and portfolio construction. It aims to provide its readers with a sound understanding of the ideas that underlie modern portfolio theory while enabling their translation to practice in markets that are dominated by noise.

The following R packages were developed specifically to support this book and its reproducibility character, and are downloadable from CRAN  [https://cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org):

- `PCRA`: Portfolio construction and risk analysis
- `facmodCS`: Cross-section factor models
- `facmodTS`: Time-series factor models
- `robustGarch`: Robust Garch(1, 1) models.
